title: IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), 2023 update
claims: The 2023 IOC consensus defines energy availability as energy intake minus exercise energy expenditure, divided by fat-free mass per day.
Reported prevalence of low energy availability or REDs indicators ranges from 23% to 79.5% in female athletes and 15% to 70% in male athletes.
The consensus distinguishes low energy availability that is adaptable from problematic low energy availability.
Problematic low energy availability is associated with reduced musculoskeletal health, increased injury risk and impaired performance.
license: BMJ copyright; citation and summary only

verification.note: BJSM 页面标注 Free，已读 Introduction、Box 1（Definitions）等正文，核对公式、患病率与 LEA 分类原文。

claimVerification.note: 原文 Box 1：“EA [Energy Availability] = {EI [Dietary energy Intake (kcal)] − EEE [Exercise Energy Expenditure (kcal)]} / FFM [Fat-Free Mass (kg) / day]”。
原文 Introduction：“the reported estimated prevalence of LEA/REDs indicators in female (23%–79.5%) and male (15%–70%) athletes”。区间完全一致。

原文 Box 1：“LEA occurs as a continuum between scenarios in which effects are benign (adaptable LEA) and others in which there are substantial and potentially long-term impairments of health and performance (problematic LEA)”。

原文 Box 1（REDs 定义）：detrimental outcomes include “decreases in… musculoskeletal health… which can all individually and synergistically lead to impaired well-being, increased injury risk and decreased sports performance”。claim 用“associated with”比原文因果链更弱，未夸大。
